cases.name: doc-json-size-at-limit-valid
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid padded with trailing spaces to exactly 4,194,304 bytes.

cases.name: doc-json-size-over-limit
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid padded to 4,194,305 bytes, one over the limit. Control: doc-json-size-at-limit-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-size-counts-utf8-bytes-at-limit-valid
cases.note: Description holds three U+1F600, 4 UTF-8 bytes each; the input is exactly 4,194,304 bytes.

cases.name: doc-json-size-counts-utf8-bytes-over-limit
cases.note: 4,194,305 bytes, but only 4,194,299 UTF-16 code units and 4,194,296 code points, so a reader that counts characters instead of bytes accepts it. Control: doc-json-size-counts-utf8-bytes-at-limit-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-bom-accepted
cases.note: One leading UTF-8 byte order mark EF BB BF before doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-bom-counted-at-limit-valid
cases.note: BOM plus document plus spaces is exactly 4,194,304 bytes.

cases.name: doc-json-bom-counted-over-limit
cases.note: BOM plus document plus spaces is 4,194,305 bytes; without the BOM it would be 4,194,302 bytes, under the limit, so this fails only when the BOM is counted. Control: doc-json-bom-counted-at-limit-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-two-boms-malformed
cases.note: A reader ignores one leading BOM; the second U+FEFF is not JSON whitespace (RFC 8259 §2). Control: doc-json-bom-accepted.

cases.name: doc-json-bom-after-whitespace-malformed
cases.note: The BOM is not leading, so it stays in the text and is not JSON whitespace. Control: doc-json-bom-accepted.

cases.name: doc-json-utf16-encoded-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid encoded as UTF-16LE with its BOM; FF is never valid in UTF-8.

cases.name: doc-json-utf8-four-byte-valid
cases.note: Description holds U+1F600 as the valid 4-byte sequence F0 9F 98 80; the control for the invalid UTF-8 cases.

cases.name: doc-json-utf8-noncharacter-valid
cases.note: EF BF BF is U+FFFF, a noncharacter but a valid UTF-8 scalar value, and allowed in an RFC 8259 string.

cases.name: doc-json-invalid-utf8-byte-ff-malformed
cases.note: Description holds invalid UTF-8: FF never occurs in UTF-8 (RFC 3629 §4). Control: doc-json-utf8-four-byte-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-invalid-utf8-overlong-malformed
cases.note: Description holds invalid UTF-8: C0 80 is an overlong encoding of U+0000 (RFC 3629 §4). Control: doc-json-utf8-four-byte-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-invalid-utf8-encoded-surrogate-malformed
cases.note: Description holds invalid UTF-8: ED A0 80 encodes the surrogate U+D800, which UTF-8 excludes (RFC 3629 §4). Control: doc-json-utf8-four-byte-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-invalid-utf8-above-max-malformed
cases.note: Description holds invalid UTF-8: F4 90 80 80 would encode U+110000, above U+10FFFF (RFC 3629 §4). Control: doc-json-utf8-four-byte-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-invalid-utf8-truncated-malformed
cases.note: Description holds invalid UTF-8: E2 82 is a 3-byte sequence cut short by the closing quote (RFC 3629 §4). Control: doc-json-utf8-four-byte-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-invalid-utf8-lone-continuation-malformed
cases.note: Description holds invalid UTF-8: 80 is a continuation byte with no lead byte (RFC 3629 §4). Control: doc-json-utf8-four-byte-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-top-level-array-malformed
cases.note: The top-level value must be an object. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-top-level-string-malformed
cases.note: The top-level value must be an object. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-top-level-number-malformed
cases.note: The top-level value must be an object. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-top-level-null-malformed
cases.note: The top-level value must be an object. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-top-level-boolean-malformed
cases.note: The top-level value must be an object. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-top-level-array-of-document-malformed
cases.note: A valid document wrapped in an array has a top-level value that is not an object.

cases.name: doc-json-empty-malformed
cases.note: Zero bytes are no JSON value.

cases.name: doc-json-whitespace-only-malformed
cases.note: Whitespace alone is no JSON value.

cases.name: doc-json-bom-only-malformed
cases.note: After the ignored BOM no JSON value remains.

cases.name: doc-json-trailing-comma-object-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a trailing comma after the last member (§json). Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §4.

cases.name: doc-json-trailing-comma-array-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a trailing comma after the last array element (§json). Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §5.

cases.name: doc-json-line-comment-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a // comment (§json). Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §2.

cases.name: doc-json-block-comment-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a /* */ comment (§json). Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §2.

cases.name: doc-json-single-quoted-string-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a single-quoted string. Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §7.

cases.name: doc-json-unquoted-key-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with an unquoted key. Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §4.

cases.name: doc-json-leading-zero-number-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a number with a leading zero, which RFC 8259 §6 excludes. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-plus-sign-number-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a number with a leading +, which RFC 8259 §6 excludes. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-nan-literal-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with the literal NaN. Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §6.

cases.name: doc-json-uppercase-literal-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with the literal True, where RFC 8259 §3 has only lowercase true. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-trailing-value-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a second value after the document. Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §2.

cases.name: doc-json-unterminated-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a missing closing brace. Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §4.

cases.name: doc-json-raw-control-character-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with an unescaped U+0001 inside a string, which RFC 8259 §7 requires to be escaped. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-raw-tab-in-string-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with an unescaped tab inside a string, which RFC 8259 §7 requires to be escaped. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-invalid-escape-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with the escape \x, which RFC 8259 §7 does not define. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-short-unicode-escape-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with a \u escape with two hex digits instead of four. Control: doc-minimal-valid. Grammar: RFC 8259 §7.

cases.name: doc-json-nbsp-whitespace-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with U+00A0 between tokens, which is not one of the four RFC 8259 §2 whitespace characters. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-form-feed-whitespace-malformed
cases.note: doc-minimal-valid with U+000C between tokens, which is not one of the four RFC 8259 §2 whitespace characters. Control: doc-minimal-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid
cases.note: A paired escape \ud83d\ude00 is U+1F600; the control for the unpaired surrogate cases.

cases.name: doc-json-escaped-nul-valid
cases.note: An escaped U+0000 is a valid string character under RFC 8259 §7; nothing in §json rejects it in a document.

cases.name: doc-json-escaped-noncharacter-valid
cases.note: U+FFFF is not a surrogate, so the string is not malformed.

cases.name: doc-json-unpaired-surrogate-lone-high-malformed
cases.note: Description is "\ud800", which contains an unpaired surrogate. Control: doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-unpaired-surrogate-lone-low-malformed
cases.note: Description is "\udc00", which contains an unpaired surrogate. Control: doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-unpaired-surrogate-reversed-pair-malformed
cases.note: Description is "\udc00\ud800", which contains an unpaired surrogate. Control: doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-unpaired-surrogate-high-before-ascii-malformed
cases.note: Description is "\ud800x", which contains an unpaired surrogate. Control: doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-unpaired-surrogate-two-highs-malformed
cases.note: Description is "\ud800\ud800", which contains an unpaired surrogate. Control: doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-unpaired-surrogate-in-key-malformed
cases.note: A key is a string, so a key with an unpaired surrogate makes the document malformed; MalformedDocument is then the only error, though the key is also unknown.

cases.name: doc-json-depth-64-arrays-not-malformed
cases.note: The top-level object is level 1 and X holds 63 nested arrays, so the deepest level is 64, which is allowed. No valid document can nest this deep, so the one defect is the unknown key X.

cases.name: doc-json-depth-65-arrays-malformed
cases.note: X holds 64 nested arrays, so the deepest level is 65. MalformedDocument is the only error. Control: doc-json-depth-64-arrays-not-malformed.

cases.name: doc-json-depth-64-objects-not-malformed
cases.note: X holds 63 nested objects, so the deepest level is 64.

cases.name: doc-json-depth-65-objects-malformed
cases.note: X holds 64 nested objects, so the deepest level is 65. Control: doc-json-depth-64-objects-not-malformed.

cases.name: doc-json-depth-64-mixed-not-malformed
cases.note: X holds 31 arrays each containing an object, then an empty array: 63 containers below the top-level object, so the deepest level is 64.

cases.name: doc-json-depth-65-mixed-malformed
cases.note: X holds 32 arrays each containing an object, the innermost holding the number 1: 64 containers below the top-level object, so the deepest level is 65. Arrays and objects both count. Control: doc-json-depth-64-mixed-not-malformed.

cases.name: doc-json-huge-exponent-not-malformed
cases.note: The magnitude of a number never makes a document malformed, so the one defect is the unknown key X.

cases.name: doc-json-long-precision-not-malformed
cases.note: Neither precision nor magnitude makes a document malformed, so the one defect is the unknown key X.

cases.name: doc-json-escaped-key-matches
cases.note: Keys match after JSON escapes are decoded, so Publishe\u0072 is Publisher and \u0052ules is Rules.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-first-valid
cases.note: Description is "\uD800\uDC00", a paired escape for U+10000, the lowest supplementary code point, with both halves at the bottom of their ranges (RFC 8259 §7, decoded as RFC 2781 §2.2 states); RFC 8259 §7 allows uppercase hex digits in an escape. Control for the unpaired surrogate cases, like doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-first-key-unknown
cases.note: The top-level key "\uD800\uDC00" decodes to U+10000, an unknown key; the pointer holds that one code point. The control of doc-json-surrogate-pair-first-key-duplicate.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-first-key-duplicate
cases.note: The top-level object has two keys, the escape "\uD800\uDC00", then U+10000 written literally in UTF-8 (F0 90 80 80); keys match after escapes are decoded, so the key repeats, and only DuplicateKey is reported though the key is also unknown (§errors). Control: doc-json-surrogate-pair-first-key-unknown.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-low-dfff-valid
cases.note: Description is "\uD800\uDFFF", a paired escape for U+103FF, the low half at the top of its range (RFC 8259 §7, decoded as RFC 2781 §2.2 states); RFC 8259 §7 allows uppercase hex digits in an escape. Control for the unpaired surrogate cases, like doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-low-dfff-key-unknown
cases.note: The top-level key "\uD800\uDFFF" decodes to U+103FF, an unknown key; the pointer holds that one code point. The control of doc-json-surrogate-pair-low-dfff-key-duplicate.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-low-dfff-key-duplicate
cases.note: The top-level object has two keys, the escape "\uD800\uDFFF", then U+103FF written literally in UTF-8 (F0 90 8F BF); keys match after escapes are decoded, so the key repeats, and only DuplicateKey is reported though the key is also unknown (§errors). Control: doc-json-surrogate-pair-low-dfff-key-unknown.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-high-dbff-valid
cases.note: Description is "\uDBFF\uDC00", a paired escape for U+10FC00, the high half at the top of its range (RFC 8259 §7, decoded as RFC 2781 §2.2 states); RFC 8259 §7 allows uppercase hex digits in an escape. Control for the unpaired surrogate cases, like doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-high-dbff-key-unknown
cases.note: The top-level key "\uDBFF\uDC00" decodes to U+10FC00, an unknown key; the pointer holds that one code point. The control of doc-json-surrogate-pair-high-dbff-key-duplicate.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-high-dbff-key-duplicate
cases.note: The top-level object has two keys, U+10FC00 written literally in UTF-8 (F4 8F B0 80), then as the escape "\uDBFF\uDC00"; keys match after escapes are decoded, so the key repeats, and only DuplicateKey is reported though the key is also unknown (§errors). Control: doc-json-surrogate-pair-high-dbff-key-unknown.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-last-valid
cases.note: Description is "\uDBFF\uDFFF", a paired escape for U+10FFFF, the highest code point, with both halves at the top of their ranges (RFC 8259 §7, decoded as RFC 2781 §2.2 states); RFC 8259 §7 allows uppercase hex digits in an escape. Control for the unpaired surrogate cases, like doc-json-surrogate-pair-valid.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-last-key-unknown
cases.note: The top-level key "\uDBFF\uDFFF" decodes to U+10FFFF, an unknown key; the pointer holds that one code point. The control of doc-json-surrogate-pair-last-key-duplicate.

cases.name: doc-json-surrogate-pair-last-key-duplicate
cases.note: The top-level object has two keys, the escape "\uDBFF\uDFFF", then U+10FFFF written literally in UTF-8 (F4 8F BF BF); keys match after escapes are decoded, so the key repeats, and only DuplicateKey is reported though the key is also unknown (§errors). Control: doc-json-surrogate-pair-last-key-unknown.
